To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a resource binding algorithm that minimizes the maximum temperature of a design can achieve significant temperature reduction, and (2) a temperature-aware resource allocation algorithm can achieve even greater temperature reduction than a temperature-aware binding algorithm.

(1) the maximum attainable temperature in a design can be reduced significantly by a temperature-aware resource allocation, (2) a temperature-aware binding can further reduce the maximum temperature in a design, and (3) a temperature-aware resource binding can reduce the maximum attainable power in a design by 10% compared to a binding optimized for power.
temperature-aware allocation and binding algorithms can significantly reduce the temperature in a design, and therefore, can be used to prevent hot spots.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a temperature-aware design methodology, which is able to reduce the impact of temperature on reliability and performance of future integrated circuits.
the development of temperature-aware high-level synthesis algorithms and techniques.
the development of temperature-aware resource allocation algorithms that can be integrated into high-level synthesis flows.

temperature-aware resource allocation is a promising approach for reducing the maximum temperature of a circuit.

our algorithms are able to provide a temperature-aware binding that is able to reduce the peak attained temperature by up to 20% and that is able to provide a binding that is within 5% of the switching power optimized binding.
temperature-aware resource allocation is feasible in high-level synthesis and that temperature can be reduced by 5% to 19% with a negligible performance impact.

we have developed a methodology for temperature-aware synthesis and that our techniques are effective in reducing maximum temperatures.

temperature-awareness in high-level synthesis is feasible and that the impact on performance can be limited.
